The ending feels entirely natural and earned because it reaches the exact thematic and emotional climax the entire piece has been building toward. The title ("Price Lookup"), the narrator's internalized produce codes, her comment at the first dinner about wearing a sweater at the register by the door, and Miss Emily's mysterious, hyper-specific "editing" of the narrator's habits all converge in the final grocery store scene. By revealing that Miss Emily also worked as a cashier for years before starting her real estate career in 1988, the ending resolves the central tension between the two women, recontextualizes Miss Emily's tough love as hard-won mentorship, and concludes with a quiet, resonant image that honors their shared working-class roots.
